## [2026-10-23](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-23.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [BeNice! Closing Looping's Inference-Memory Gap via KV-Sharing](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31633>)

BeNice adds an auxiliary fine-tuning objective that makes a looped language model’s early pass compatible with the final pass’s cached keys and values, enabling the recurrences to share one history cache. On the tested Parcae models, it largely preserves the quality of ordinary fine-tuning while removing the recurrence-dependent cache duplication, offering a way to increase inference depth without proportional growth in cache memory.

**Published:** 2026-10-22 · **First seen:** 2026-10-23T10:03:45.396Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Looped Models, KV Sharing, Auxiliary Loss, LoRA

**Public availability:** 2026-10-23T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.LG/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.31633v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Pinned v1 PDF (37 pages), HTML main methods/results and relevant evaluation, convergence, LoRA and training appendices inspected. The primary novelty is supervised adaptation, hence category1.5 rather than the application category3.4. Stochastic-depth pretraining uses per-sequence Poisson recurrence depth; the new objective combines ordinary final-recurrence cross-entropy with an auxiliary hybrid predictor using first-recurrence queries/residuals and final-recurrence KV. This avoids training through complete sequential shared-cache rollouts. The diagnosis localizes failures in released770M/1.3B Parcae models to a low-rank first-layer/first-recurrence residual shift; stochastic-depth convergence alone does not ensure the same shared/unshared fixed point. Full fine-tuning uses140M tokens; a rank8 first-layer key/value LoRA variant uses65M tokens and41K/49K trainable parameters. Table5 compares independently tuned standard fine-tuning and BeNice over three seeds: released770M shared validation perplexity21.61→11.86 while unshared remains11.86 versus11.85; the1.3B shared result18.52→10.78 accompanies unshared10.79 for both. Newly pretrained140M–1.3B models and22-task Core/46-task Core-Extended suites support the mechanism; the new370M shared Core score rises15.16→23.51. Section5.3 separately reports1.3B Parcae global HBM63.82→21.60GB at batch64/context2048 (weights, cache, graphs and buffers included), and proxy looped-model Mooncake/AIPerf workload experiments: at2requests/s cache hits rise8.1percentage points, throughput23.6%, and p90 time to first token139.2→23.2seconds. These serving proxies are distinct from the quality-tested BeNice models. Receipt is2026-10-22T17:49:44Z; the original FridayOct23 cs.LG batch plus official Thursday20:00US/Eastern posting schedule imply announcement2026-10-23T00:00Z, within this daily window. Earlier looped KV sharing and Parcae checkpoints are background, not claimed as new. No earlier BeNice release or author implementation/project destination was verified in the inspected primary text and exact-title search.

**Limitations:** The empirical adaptation results concern140M–1.3B Parcae-family models, finite task suites and mostly2048-token training contexts; they do not establish quality preservation for arbitrary looped architectures, frontier models or all context lengths. The convergence theorem assumes a contractive recurrent block and Lipschitz KV projections; stochastic-depth training is not proven to make every model contractive. First-layer localization/mean patching is not universal across all newly trained models, and Kimi delta-attention variants already share state well without extra adaptation. Prelude/coda caches remain, so total KV is not reduced by exactly1/T, and recurrences still consume computation. Low-precision composition is a quality study, not an independently measured FP4 kernel speedup. The serving section explicitly simulates the memory-constrained regime with proxies constructed by looping existing weights such as GLM4.7-FP8; their downstream quality is not shown to match BeNice-trained models, and serving GPU type/count is not specified in the inspected setup. Low-load workloads show little latency/throughput gain. No general production or quality-preserving frontier serving speedup, public BeNice code release, or independent reproduction is claimed.

## [2026-10-20](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-20.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Self-Distillation for Supervised Fine-Tuning](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25497>)

Gold-Conditioned Distillation replaces one-hot fine-tuning targets with soft predictions from an exponentially averaged copy of the model that can see the correct response in its prompt. Both models follow the fixed gold response without generating training rollouts, and the new study finds better target-task learning with modest average retention gains, suggesting a practical alternative to ordinary supervised fine-tuning.

**Published:** 2026-10-18 · **First seen:** 2026-10-21T10:02:45.546Z · **Novelty:** material-update · **Tags:** Gold-Conditioned Distillation, Soft Targets, Capability Retention

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25497v1>) · [Code](<https://github.com/WenxuanZhu1103/gcd>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Pinned v1 Sections 3–5 and Appendices A–F inspected. A gold-revealed EMA teacher (update rate0.01) supplies forward-KL targets on exactly the same gold-response prefixes seen by the student; neither model samples completions during training. Four backbones span Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, Qwen3-4B-Base, Llama3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen3-8B-Base, with full tuning at3–4B and rank64 LoRA at8B. Table8’s five-seed Tooluse study reports GCD66.7±0.6 versus SFT61.1±0.7 on Qwen2.5-3B and69.6±0.5 versus63.2±0.6 on Qwen3-4B; Llama gains are smaller. Main tasks also cover scientific MCQ and LiveNews; previous capability is measured on five general benchmarks. Shared four-epoch A10080GB pipelines, label-smoothing/base-KL comparisons and EMA/KL-direction ablations provide controls. This new detailed paper and controlled evaluation were announced in the October20 CL batch; the compact author implementation existed earlier, so the entry is a material paper update rather than a new-code release.

**Limitations:** Retention gains are modest and individual metrics can regress, including instruction following. LiveNews trains on paraphrased versions of the same facts tested with original questions; this is phrasing transfer after knowledge injection, not generalization to unseen facts. Main comparisons use matched settings but not exhaustive per-method tuning; SDFT is reproduced with a forward-KL modification, and its learning-rate sweep covers only selected cases. Multi-seed results cover Tooluse and three models, not every task/backbone. Soft targets add a teacher forward and EMA storage even though they avoid autoregressive rollouts; no universal wall-time saving is measured. Released compact code covers Tooluse/LiveNews on the two smaller Qwen models, not the full paper experiment suite. All models are at most8B; no independent reproduction.

**Update:** 2026-10-20: The newly announced full paper adds four-backbone target-task/retention comparisons, a five-seed Tooluse study and EMA/KL/soft-label ablations to the earlier compact GCD implementation (https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25497v1; https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/recent?skip=0&amp;show=2000; https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html). The author repository’s single October18 commit contains a compact training implementation and data rather than these controlled study results (https://github.com/WenxuanZhu1103/gcd; https://api.github.com/repos/WenxuanZhu1103/gcd/git/trees/main?recursive=1; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WenxuanZhu1103/gcd/main/README.md). Git creation/commit dates do not establish exact first public visibility. Preserve October18 as the paper’s receipt date; October20T00Z refers only to its schedule-inferred paper announcement, not a reset of method/code age.

## [2026-10-04](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-04.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Finetuning with Sampling: SFT Learns Better Than You Think](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02140>)

Projection sampling rewrites expert solutions using a frozen learner and selects revisions that better fit its response distribution before ordinary supervised fine-tuning. The prepared data improve task learning and prior-skill retention in several tested settings, offering a way to adapt the training data while retaining the standard SFT objective.

**Published:** 2026-10-01 · **First seen:** 2026-10-03T16:42:52Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** SFT, Projection Sampling, Knowledge Retention

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02140>) · [Project](<https://aakaran.github.io/finetuning_with_sampling/>) · [Code](<https://github.com/aakaran/finetuning-with-sampling>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Experiments cover math, scientific skills, and open-ended expertise with 3B/7B models, including forgetting measurements and sampling ablations. Submission: 2026-10-01T17:45:07Z; the cs.CL listing confirms the October 2 public batch. First examined for a separate October 3 handout after that day's report cutoff; absent from all 74 registry entries, so this is delayed first daily coverage.

**Limitations:** The released sampler greedily improves mean token log-likelihood; it does not implement the exact Metropolis-Hastings acceptance ratio. Expert-information preservation is imperfect, offline sampling has substantial cost, and comparisons do not establish equal end-to-end compute. Results vary by task and model; the method does not uniformly beat on-policy baselines.

### [AstaBrief: citation-focused SFT and preference training for scientific reports](<https://allenai.org/blog/astabrief>)

AstaBrief adapts Qwen3-8B to write cited scientific reports from already retrieved literature snippets in one pass, using citation-filtered supervised examples and agreement-filtered preference pairs. The released weights and training recipe provide a practical starting point for faster evidence-grounded synthesis, with comparisons limited to the older models and report workflows used during development.

**Published:** 2026-10-02 · **First seen:** 2026-10-03T10:04:56Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Scientific Synthesis, Citation Grounding, Preference Optimization

[Blog](<https://allenai.org/blog/astabrief>) · [Project](<https://huggingface.co/allenai/AstaBrief_8B>) · [Code](<https://github.com/allenai/ai2-scholarqa-lib/tree/main/api/scholarqa/lite>)

**Evidence:** technical-report; full-text. The October 2 technical disclosure describes 47K supervised examples and about 6K preference pairs, with citation-density filtering producing the strongest filtering gains. The model card reports citation recall rising from 64.6 for Qwen3-8B to 78.2 for AstaBrief on the 100-question SQABench-CS2 test split. The blog reports 51.1 versus 178.5 seconds across the full Fast/Thinking pipelines, about 3.5 times faster. This is first coverage of the newly published technical write-up; model development largely predates this release. Ai2 and its official mirror date the disclosure October 2 without a verified hour; it is eligible within the 72-hour lookback but conservatively labeled newly-discovered because its position relative to the 10:00 UTC main-window boundary is uncertain.

**Limitations:** Most training and evaluation occurred in 2025 and were not rerun against current frontier models. Evidence relies heavily on model judges; the human study covers only 14 questions. Pipeline latency compares different workflows, not an isolated model substitution, and citation scores do not fully measure preservation of scientific claim scope. No independent reproduction. Model weights use Apache 2.0, while the verified DPO dataset uses CC-BY-NC-4.0.

## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [LoRA Without Regret](<https://thinkingmachines.ai/blog/lora/>)

This experimental study examines when low-rank adaptation can match full fine-tuning by varying adapter rank, training-set size, batch size, learning rate, and the layers being adapted. It gives practitioners a concrete recipe for efficient adaptation, including sufficient adapter capacity and coverage of feed-forward layers, while identifying large-data and large-batch regimes where gaps remain.

**Published:** 2025-09-29 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:09:33Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** LoRA, Fine-tuning, Hyperparameters

**Positioning:** established-method

[Blog](<https://thinkingmachines.ai/blog/lora/>)

**Evidence:** technical-report; full-text. The report sweeps rank and learning rates on Llama and Qwen models using instruction and reasoning data, and separately tests mathematical reinforcement learning.

**Limitations:** Supervised comparisons primarily use log loss rather than broad downstream generation metrics; the findings apply to tested post-training regimes and do not guarantee equivalence for pretraining-like data volumes.
